newsitem.title: KENYA: Bill rates continue down at Kenyan auction.
newsitem.headline: Bill rates continue down at Kenyan auction.

text.p: Rates on treasury bills fell again at this week's auction as the Central Bank of Kenya continued to showcase its commitment to cutting overall interest rates.
The central bank accepted only around 1.489 billion shillings of treasury bills out of 9.0 billion it tendered.
The bank said that it offered an average interest rate of 22.497 percent percent for its main category 91-day treasury bills compared to 23.424 in the previous week.
It offered an unchanged 15.005 percent on 28-day bills. No investors tendered for 182-day bills for which rates offered the previous week were 20.070 percent.
The bank said average interest rates tendered for were 16.728 percent for 28-day bills and 23.212 percent for 91-day bills. There were rates as high as around 27 percent tendered.
"Our cut level appears very low again this week but that is due to our commitment to keeping the interest rates down," a central bank official said. "This is a matter of policy."
The official would not say whether the central bank tactics would continue next week, when it has invited 5.0 billion shillings in treasury bills to be submitted by Thursday.
Of the amounts accepted, 21.1 million shillings was for 28-day bills while 1.468 billion was for 91-day bills.

Last week, the central bank accepted only 321.95 million shillings of treasury bills from a total 9.0 billion shillings it tendered. An official said some investors had asked for "ridiculous" interest rates which it would not encourage.
Commercial bank lending rates currently range in the 24-30 percent range. Interest on deposits is around 10-16 percent.
